bib.title: OpenCoder: The Open Cookbook for Top-Tier Code Large Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only (lineage); everything else read.

question: Can a code LLM that is competitive with leading open-weight models be built from a fully released, reproducible data pipeline, and which data-curation choices matter at each training stage?
hypothesis: Heuristic cleaning, file-level deduplication, recall of code-related web text and high-quality synthetic data in annealing and SFT are the key ingredients of a top-tier code LLM.
contributions: Release of OpenCoder 1.5B and 8B (base and instruct) with intermediate checkpoints
RefineCode, a 960B-token reproducible pretraining corpus over 607 languages with 130+ rules
Large-scale SFT corpus and data processing pipeline
Ablations on dedup level, annealing data quality, GitHub stars and two-stage SFT

method.summary: Builds RefineCode (cleaned GitHub code plus code-related web text), pretrains 1.5B and 8B decoder models with a WSD schedule and a short annealing phase on high-quality and synthetic data, then runs two-stage SFT. Ablations train 1.5B models on Python-only or full-mix variants and track HumanEval/MBPP Pass@1 curves.
method.task: code LLM pretraining, annealing and instruction tuning

datasets.name: RefineCode
datasets.size: 960B tokens (about 730B tokens after downsampling, used in pretraining stage)
datasets.source: GitHub repositories up to November 2023, non-GitHub data from The Stack v2, web recall from Common Crawl, SkyPile, FineWeb, AutoMathText
datasets.preprocessing: files over 8 MB dropped; 607 language types kept; exact (SHA256) then fuzzy dedup (5-gram, 2048 MinHash, LSH 16 bands x 128 rows, removes 6% file volume); copyright removal; PII replacement; 130+ heuristic filters; Java 449GB to 200GB, HTML 474GB to 64GB

datasets.name: Code-related web data
datasets.size: about 220GB from Common Crawl after 3 iterations, 330GB total across corpora, plus 178GB from GitHub text
datasets.source: fastText classifier seeded with 500,000 annotated code-like pages (Autonomous Data Selection)
datasets.preprocessing: BPE-segmented text for fastText; domains with over 10% recalled pages marked code-related; manual URL annotation

datasets.name: Annealing mix
datasets.size: RefineCode 83.94B, Algorithmic Corpus 12.44B, High Quality Code Snippet 2.71B, Code Textbooks 0.91B tokens
datasets.source: Algorithmic corpus sampled by keywords leetcode, def solution, class solution; snippets with tests; textbooks via Qwen2-72B-Instruct on hqcode

datasets.name: SFT stage 1
datasets.size: RealUser-Instruct 0.7M, Large-scale Diverse-Instruct 2.3M, Filtered Infinity-Instruct 1.0M examples
datasets.preprocessing: strict dedup; entry points of HumanEval/MBPP removed; 10-gram overlap removal

datasets.name: SFT stage 2
datasets.source: open and synthesized code instruction data
datasets.preprocessing: synthesized Python tasks kept only if test cases pass

datasets.name: HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench, LiveCodeBench, MultiPL-E, McEval, MdEval, CodeArena
datasets.size: MBPP 500 questions (3-shot), 378 sanitized for EvalPlus; CodeArena nearly 400 samples; LiveCodeBench split 2305-2409

models.name: OpenCoder-1.5B
models.tokenizer: citation broken in text ('using the tokenizer proposed in ?')

models.name: OpenCoder-8B
models.heads: 32 (8 KV heads) per Table 4; text says 8 attention heads

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, Yi-Coder, StarCoder2, CodeGemma, CodeLlama, Crystal

training.lr: peak 3e-4 (pretraining), decayed to 1e-5 in annealing; SFT stage 1 2e-5, stage 2 5e-5
training.lr_schedule: WSD (MiniCPM): constant after warmup, exponential decay to 1e-5 in annealing; cosine for SFT
training.warmup: 2,000 steps over 8B tokens (pretraining); 100 steps (each SFT stage)
training.batch_size: global 1024 (micro-batch 4 for 1.5B, 1 for 8B); 8B first 130,000 steps used global 2048 at seq 4096; SFT stage 1 4096, stage 2 512
training.epochs: 1.5B: 4 epochs over 2T tokens; 8B: 3.5 epochs over 2.5T tokens; SFT stage 1 one epoch, stage 2 three epochs

other.ablation models: 1.5B, ablations trained up to roughly 100B tokens on curves read from Figs 8-11 (axis 0-100B); RefineCode vs Stack v2 comparison at 600B tokens
other.note: 1.5B lacked code-related recall data due to incomplete data curation

inference.temperature: 1.0 for question generation in large-scale diverse instruction synthesis; evaluation temperature not stated

other.eval framework: OpenCodeEval for base models; Qwen2.5-Coder evaluation code for MultiPL-E

metrics.name: Pass@1
metrics.definition: fraction of problems solved by a generated solution passing unit tests

metrics.name: CodeArena win rate
metrics.definition: win rate against GPT-4 baseline, GPT-4 judge, nearly 400 human-written prompts

prompts.text: You are a teaching assistant helping to create a Python programming task from a given code snippet. You must provide the best response to the Python programming task, including reasoning thought, reference solutions, explanation of test cases, and test code.
You are an expert in designing high-quality programming questions based on the given text.
